clue.text: Crazy plan helpful officer put in

indicators.note: put in tells us the officer's letters are placed inside the plan's

parts.note: a plan or chart can be a map
ADC is an aide-de-camp, an officer who assists a senior commander

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses a wild scheme that an obliging officer submitted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put in' sounds like submitting the plan, but it is the container signal; an ADC (aide-de-camp) is a senior officer's personal assistant.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone wildly impulsive or reckless.

clue.text: Lovely party held in fields

indicators.note: held in means the party is placed inside the fields word

parts.note: arable land is farmland for crops, hence fields
a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: A delightful celebration takes place out in the meadows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fields' is the adjective for cropland standing in for the land itself, a common crossword stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean charming or delightful.

clue.text: Entertainment unfinished — admit disappointment

indicators.note: unfinished drops the final letter of the entertainment word

parts.note: a comedy is a form of entertainment
to own or own up is to admit

explanation.surface: A show is left incomplete and someone confesses their letdown.
explanation.definitionFit: A fall in status or an anticlimax: a letdown.

clue.text: One dependent on receiving pounds or pennies

indicators.note: pounds is a verb here, as beating something into a new shape

explanation.surface: Someone relies on income in pounds or pence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pounds' looks like money beside 'pennies', but it is the verb to batter, rearranging OR PENNIES.
explanation.definitionFit: A retired person relies on a regular state or company payment for income.

clue.text: Beetle's sick feeling

definitions.meaning: to beetle is to jut out or overhang, as beetling brows do
the queasy aftermath of too much drink

explanation.surface: An insect is apparently feeling unwell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beetle' looks like the insect; here it is the verb meaning to project or overhang, and the 's is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The rough morning after heavy drinking is the familiar sense; overhang is the verb sense.

clue.text: One old man, all charm — unusual in a statesman

indicators.note: unusual signals the letters are to be arranged in an unusual order

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A political leader is pictured as an old fellow full of charm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a' is a link. 'Unusual' shuffles I with OLDMANALLCHARM. He was British Prime Minister 1957 to 1963, an elderly, urbane figure nicknamed Supermac.
explanation.definitionFit: This Conservative served as British Prime Minister, a leading political figure.

clue.text: Slow to develop chant book

definitions.meaning: happening little by little, step by step
a book of the sung responses of the Mass, the chants between Epistle and Gospel

explanation.surface: A hymnal that takes its time to come together.
explanation.walkthrough: In church use the second sense is a liturgical book of chants, named from the altar steps where they were sung.
explanation.definitionFit: Step-by-step progress is the familiar sense; the liturgical one names a book of Mass chants.

clue.text: Man entitled to reckon bombs are over

indicators.note: are over in a down clue means the bombs sit above the reckon word

parts.note: V1s were the German flying bombs of the Second World War
to count is to reckon

explanation.surface: Someone works out that the bombing raids have ended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Are over' sounds like an all-clear; in a down answer it puts VIS above COUNT. 'To' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A nobleman ranking between earl and baron holds a title, so he is a titled man.

clue.text: Reserved enclosure in which formal procedure is drawn up

indicators.note: in which tells us the enclosure contains the other piece

parts.note: a ring is an enclosure, as a boxing ring or show ring

indicators.note: drawn up in a down clue means the word is pulled upwards, so read backwards

parts.note: a rite is a formal ceremony or procedure

explanation.surface: An area set apart where official protocols are drafted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawn up' sounds like drafting a document; in a down answer it reads the ceremony word upwards, giving ETIR.
explanation.definitionFit: Shy and withdrawn: reserved in manner.

clue.text: It's more normal for the ordinary undergraduate

definitions.meaning: the comparative of an adjective meaning usual or everyday
at Oxford and some other universities, a student without a scholarship or exhibition is so called

explanation.surface: A remark that average students are more typical.
explanation.walkthrough: At Oxford a student who holds no scholarship is traditionally called a commoner; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as a comparative it means more frequent; as a noun it is a fee-paying student without a scholarship.

clue.text: Team of lawyers chronicled county

parts.note: barristers collectively are the Bar
a set is a group or team of players

explanation.surface: A law firm's team wrote a history of the shire.
explanation.walkthrough: Anthony Trollope's novels 'The Chronicles of Barsetshire' are set in this invented English county.
explanation.definitionFit: Trollope's novel series records life in this fictional cathedral shire, so it is the county with chronicles.

clue.text: Person wrongly holds physician to be a baboon

indicators.note: holds means the person-and-wrongly pair grips the doctor between its parts

parts.note: a man is a person
ill can mean badly or wrongly, as in ill-advised
Dr is the abbreviation for doctor

explanation.surface: Someone mistakenly believes their doctor is a monkey.
explanation.definitionFit: This brightly faced West African primate is a species of baboon-like monkey.

clue.text: Fluid state of mind

definitions.meaning: one of the four bodily liquids of old medicine, such as bile or phlegm
a mood, as in good or ill temper

explanation.surface: Someone's mental state is changeable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fluid' looks like an adjective, changeable; it is a noun for an old medical body liquid.
explanation.definitionFit: Medieval medicine named four body liquids by this term, and it also means a mood or temper.

clue.text: Quixotically attacked natural power source

definitions.meaning: in Cervantes' novel Don Quixote charges at sail-driven mills, thinking them giants
a machine harnessing moving air, a renewable energy supply

explanation.surface: A romantic hero charges at a source of renewable energy.
explanation.walkthrough: In Cervantes' novel Don Quixote tilts at these, taking them for giants; they are also driven by the breeze, a natural power.
explanation.definitionFit: Sail-driven mills turned by the breeze harness nature, and the Don famously charged at them.

clue.text: One must watch what one says

definitions.text: One must watch what one says

parts.words: One must watch what one says
parts.note: read literally, a deaf person following speech by looking at the speaker's mouth

explanation.surface: Advice to be careful of one's words.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom means be careful what you say; read literally, the speaker's mouth is watched.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who understands speech by observing mouth movements must literally watch spoken words.

clue.text: This mineral layer's pronounced empty

indicators.note: pronounced means the word we hear is spelt differently from the one entered

parts.note: vain means empty or futile, as in vain promises

explanation.surface: A geologist declares a seam of ore barren.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Empty' looks like a description of the layer, but it is the synonym said aloud; 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A seam of ore running through rock is called a lode or by this word.

clue.text: No citizen wants endless foul beer

definitions.note: cryptically, one who is not a city dweller

indicators.note: endless means the last letter of the foul word is removed

parts.note: vile means foul or disgusting
lager is a kind of beer

explanation.surface: A city resident rejects a nasty drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Citizen' in its old sense is an inhabitant of a city, so a country dweller is no citizen; 'wants' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A rural dweller lives in a small settlement rather than a city, so is not a city dweller.

clue.text: Where film may be kept from public

definitions.text: Where film may be kept from public

parts.words: Where film may be kept from public
parts.note: a reel of film sits inside a photographic device; also a legal phrase for proceedings held in private

explanation.surface: A question about where footage is stored away from viewers.
explanation.walkthrough: The Latin legal phrase means in a judge's private chambers, not in open court.
explanation.definitionFit: The legal phrase means in private, with the public excluded, and literally film sits inside the device.

clue.text: Speculator sees period of growth cut short

indicators.note: cut short means the final letter of the word is lopped off

parts.note: a stage is a phase of development

explanation.surface: An investor notices that a boom has ended early.
explanation.walkthrough: On the stock market a stag buys new shares hoping to sell them quickly at a profit; 'sees' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Market slang for one who applies for new share issues to resell at once for a quick gain.

clue.text: No longer allowing use of amalgam

definitions.meaning: ceasing or bringing something to a halt
a dental filling made of mercury alloy is an old word for a tooth plug

explanation.surface: A dentist ceases to permit mercury fillings.
explanation.walkthrough: In older British usage a dental filling, often of amalgam, is called by this name.
explanation.definitionFit: Halting is the everyday sense; filling a tooth with amalgam is the dentist's old sense.

clue.text: Scare father in a punch-up

indicators.note: in tells us father's letters are placed inside the other pieces

parts.note: a punch-up is a fight
Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title

explanation.surface: A parent is frightened during a brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scare' is a verb here; the answer is an old-fashioned word for frighten.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic verb meaning to frighten or alarm.

clue.text: To split a prize appears eccentric

parts.note: to crack is to split or break
a pot is a prize or trophy, as in a sports cup

explanation.surface: Sharing a trophy is presented as a strange idea.
explanation.definitionFit: A crackpot is a crank, someone with odd or foolish ideas.

clue.text: Scientist changes end of shift

indicators.note: changes end of means the final letter of the garment word is swapped for another

parts.note: a shift is a loose dress or slip, also called a chemise

explanation.surface: A researcher changes as the working shift ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shift' looks like a work period; it is a dress, CHEMISE, whose last E is changed to T (the end of 'shift').
explanation.definitionFit: One trained in the science of substances and their reactions.

clue.text: Ferment as chairman finally goes on holiday

indicators.note: goes on means the letter follows on after the holiday word

parts.note: leave is time off work

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of chairman

explanation.surface: Unrest breaks out once the company chairman takes a vacation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goes on holiday' reads as one phrase, but 'goes on' places N after LEAVE; 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Yeast or another raising agent that makes dough ferment and rise; also used as a verb.

clue.text: Clumsy salesman about to interrupt one at head of queue

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

indicators.note: to interrupt means the turned word breaks into the middle of the other pieces

parts.note: whoever is at the front of a queue is next

indicators.note: about tells us the salesman's word is turned back to front

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative

explanation.surface: A pushy salesman barges in on the person at the front of a line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' reverses the salesman to PER; 'one at head of queue' reads as a single person but splits into the numeral and the word for who goes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking skill and so awkward or bungling, the opposite of an expert.

clue.text: Man no longer uses this sort of coffee

definitions.meaning: the Isle of Man's Celtic tongue, Manx, died out as a native language
coffee laced with whisky and topped with cream, like Irish coffee

explanation.surface: A man has given up drinking a particular brew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is the Isle of Man, whose Manx form of this Celtic language lost its last native speaker in 1974.
explanation.definitionFit: Manx is a branch of this Celtic language family, and a whisky-laced coffee bears the same name.

clue.text: Digs gold out in margins of goldfields

indicators.note: out signals the letters of gold are thrown out of order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: margins of picks the first and last letters of goldfields

explanation.surface: A prospector digs for gold around the edges of the mining area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Digs' looks like the verb of the gold rush; it is British slang for rented rooms. 'Out' rearranges GOLD into LODG.
explanation.definitionFit: Rented rooms are called digs in British slang.

clue.text: After-effects of battle on corps

definitions.note: plural in the clue; the answer is used as a mass noun for consequences

indicators.note: on means the battle word is placed after the corps letters

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army
action is fighting, as in killed in action

explanation.surface: The aftermath of combat for an army unit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' places the battle word after the corps letters; 'of' is a link. The Royal Engineers are a British Army corps.
explanation.definitionFit: A response that follows an event is its consequence or after-effect.

clue.text: Word used to approve true love

parts.note: right means correct or true
love is zero in tennis, written as the letter O

explanation.surface: A sweetheart says yes to genuine love.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheerful British expression of agreement, like okay.
